standard_prerequisites: Chapter Definition definition-set-theoretic-equivalence, included as a context span below: j is a set-theoretic pre-equivalence relation when for every algebraically closed field k over B the relation sim-R on U(k), given by u sim-R u-prime iff some field extension K over k admits a K-valued point r of R with s(r) = u and t(r) = u-prime, is an equivalence relation; j is a set-theoretic equivalence relation when it is moreover universally injective

The three induced maps of Equation equation-list: the composition map j-comp from R composed with itself over U, the diagonal map j-diag from U, and the flip map j-flip from R, all landing in U times over B U

Morphisms of Spaces, Lemma spaces-morphisms-lemma-large-enough: surjectivity statements on topological spaces can be witnessed on k-valued points as soon as the cardinality of the algebraically closed field k exceeds the bound lambda associated to R
Morphisms of Spaces, Lemmas spaces-morphisms-lemma-permanence-finite-type and spaces-morphisms-lemma-base-change-finite-type: local finite type is preserved under composition and under base change

Morphisms of Spaces, Lemma spaces-morphisms-lemma-locally-finite-type-surjective-geometric-points: a nonempty algebraic space locally of finite type over an algebraically closed field has a k-valued point
core_obligations: Assume (2) and fix an algebraically closed field k over B; show sim-R is symmetric: given a K-valued point r of R over the pair (u1, u2), the containment of the image of j-flip in the image of j produces a point r-prime of the topological space |R| with |j|(r-prime) = |j-flip|(r); since (u2, u1) lies in the equivalence class defining |j|(r-prime), a field extension K-prime over k and a morphism r-prime from Spec of K-prime to R exist with j composed with r-prime equal to (u2, u1) composed with the structure map, which is exactly the commutativity of the dotted arrows in the two-column fibre diagram; hence sim-R is symmetric
Reflexivity: the same argument with the containment of the image of j-diag in the image of j, mirroring verbatim the symmetry case just displayed

Transitivity: given u1, u2, u3 with K1 and K2 valued points r1, r2 of R connecting the consecutive pairs, choose a common over-field K containing both K1 and K2 over k, view r1 and r2 as K-valued points of R, and apply the argument of the first part to the containment of the image of j-comp in the image of j; the dotted arrows in the fibre diagram then produce a K-valued point of R over (u1, u3); hence sim-R is transitive and (2) implies (1)

(1) implies (3): assume j is a set-theoretic pre-equivalence relation and let k be algebraically closed over B with cardinality larger than lambda(R); given u sim-R u-prime there is a point of |R| over the pair (u, u-prime) in |U times B U|, and the large-enough lemma lifts it to an R(k)-valued point with j(r) = (u, u-prime)

(3) implies (2): pick any point c of the topological space of R composed with itself over U, represent it by a k-valued point with k of sufficiently large cardinality; then j-comp(c) equals j(r) for some r in R(k), hence j-comp(c) = j(r) in |U times B U|; the same argument with the diagonal and the flip maps gives the containments for j-diag and j-flip

(4) implies (3) with no hypotheses; conversely assume s and t locally of finite type and prove (1) implies (4): for u sim-R u-prime the fibre product Z of R over j with Spec of k at the pair (u, u-prime) is nonempty, and j locally of finite type makes Z locally of finite type over the algebraically closed field k by the permanence and base-change lemmas, so Z has a k-valued point by the geometric-point lemma, which is exactly (u, u-prime) in j(R(k))
proof_roadmap: Prove symmetry and transitivity of sim-R from the image containments via the fibre diagrams, noting reflexivity is the same argument with the diagonal map
Pass between the topological image containments and k-valued point statements using the cardinality lift
Handle the locally finite type refinement (1) implies (4) through the nonempty fibre product and the geometric-point lemma
